messages:
josh (support): Heads-up — ACME reporting a batch of requests routed to eu-west-1 instead of us-west-2 starting ~16:42 UTC. High latency and inflated token billing.

acme-integration-bot: Customer logs attached — shows X-Region-Preference header present (eu-west-1) and JWT claim preferred_region=us-west-2.

josh (support): They insist behavior changed after our deploy 2026-03-03-canary. Previously JWT claim took precedence.

priya (eng-runtime): :eyes: I remember a small change to routing precedence in the canary — we swapped header vs jwt ordering for some edge cases. Might be related.

sara (sre): Can we get a repro curl from them? Need exact headers + auth token.

josh (support): Got one from ACME:
```
curl -v "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <JWT>" \
  -H "X-Region-Preference: eu-west-1" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-v1","input":"hello"}'
```

acme-integration-bot: Example JWT payload (decoded): `{"sub":"acme-service","preferred_region":"us-west-2","exp":1710000000}`

priya (eng-runtime): Repro test locally: when router precedence is HEADER > JWT we pick eu-west-1. When JWT > HEADER we pick us-west-2. So the change you mentioned would explain this.

mia (infra): Which config flips precedence? I can roll back the canary if needed.

priya (eng-runtime): It's controlled by ROUTER_REGION_SOURCE_ORDER env; on canary it was set to `header,jwt,origin` instead of `jwt,header,origin`. The change was intended for compatibility but it regresses customers relying on JWT ties.

josh (support): Customer expects JWT to be authoritative for their multi-tenant routing. They hit 3x latency and a large billing delta for 2 hours. We need a mitigation and a postmortem. :fire:

sara (sre): Immediate mitigation options: 1) revert canary to previous env order 2) add ACL so ACME's requests always honor JWT 3) ask ACME to include X-Force-Region header that we treat as high-priority. Which is fastest?

priya (eng-runtime): Fastest: revert canary (mia can promote rollback to canary->stable) or set customer-specific override keyed by tenant id — but that's more work.

mia (infra): I can rollback the canary config to `jwt,header,origin` in ~15 mins. Need support ticket id and confirm scope (global vs canary).

josh (support): Ticket #SUP-12482. Please revert global canary config for region precedence to jwt-first. Customer impacted: ACME (acct: acme-prod).

priya (eng-runtime): Also adding tests — router unit tests didn't cover JWT vs header former behavior. I'll add an integration test to prevent regressions.

sara (sre): Logging note: the router emits selection annotations; see sample: `router:select region=eu-west-1 source=header prio=10 candidate_jwt=us-west-2 prio=20`. That's confusing because prio number decreased after the change. I'll patch log to include configured precedence ordering.

josh (support): ACME asked for a repro they can use to confirm fix. Provide them curl + a generated JWT and the exact header set.

priya (eng-runtime): Repro curl we validated:
```
# JWT with preferred_region=us-west-2
echo '{"sub":"acme","preferred_region":"us-west-2"}' > payload.json
# sign with our test key (example)
jwt=$(jwt-cli sign payload.json --key test-key)

curl -i \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $jwt" \
  -H "X-Region-Preference: eu-west-1" \
  https://canary.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Expected before rollback: routed to eu-west-1. Expected after rollback: routed to us-west-2.

mia (infra): Rolling back canary config now. I'll post when complete.

(30s pass)

mia (infra): Revert done — canary now uses `jwt,header,origin`. Pushed and config refreshed across edges.

priya (eng-runtime): Confirmed on canary: router log now shows `selected_region=us-west-2 source=jwt prio=20`. Integration test added to PR #3421.

josh (support): Told ACME it's reverted and to retest. They replied: "confirmed fixed — latency back to normal, billing looks right".

sara (sre): Action items: eng-runtime to open postmortem describing why precedence change was pushed without customer impact analysis; add conservatism in precedence changes. Also add tenant override ops playbook.

priya (eng-runtime): On it. I'll draft postmortem and include test additions and a changelog note about ROUTER_REGION_SOURCE_ORDER.

josh (support): Thanks all. Leaving this thread open until postmortem published and ACME confirms no billing adjustments needed. :thumbsup:
